summary: Raymond Allchin (1923–2010) was an archaeology and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of London and SOAS under K. de B. Codrington, later lecturing at SOAS (1954–1959) and holding a readership at the University of Cambridge (1972–1989).

Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied under Martin Haug (~1859–1866). He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1878–1892), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (~1892–1907).

Reb Anderson (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki (1967) and Richard Baker (~1970–1983). He succeeded Baker and served as abbot at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1986–1995).
Reb Gongwa Jamyang Chökyi Lodrö studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.

Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale, later holding posts at the University of Colorado and University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Reginald A. Ray (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Mentored by teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa, he held posts at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006) and the University of Colorado (attested 2001–2002).

Reginald Horace Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies. After studying at the University of London (~1919–1923), he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1941).
Rei Yoshimura (born 1929) is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1949–1958), where he later served as a professor (~1974–1999).
Reiho Masunaga (1902–1981) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya (~1924–1931) and held a teaching post at Komazawa University (~1930–1972).

Reiko Ohnuma is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, later holding posts at UT Austin (1996–1997), the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College (attested 2012).

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. His posts included professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (1949) and professor, later president, at Kyoto Women's University (1963).

Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and the University of Heidelberg (from 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indology scholar who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a scholar of linguistics. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831), where he served as assistant professor (1832) and extraordinary professor (1849–1870).

Reinhold Niebuhr (1892–1971) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School (~1913–1915), and held a long-term post at Union Theological Seminary (~1928–1960).

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After earning his Ph.D. at Jena under Stickel and Gildemeister, he taught at St Augustine's College and served as Head Librarian at the India Office Library (1869–1893).

Renate Syed (born 1953) is an Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982), where she studied under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renjū Akamatsu (1841–1919) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
René Gothóni (born 1950) is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1980) and later held a post there (~1975–2014).

René Grousset (1885–1952) was a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Montpellier and served at the Musée Guimet (~1925–1944) and as curator at the Musée Cernuschi (~1933–1952).
